questions.s: In the Haber process, nitrogen and hydrogen are reacted to form ammonia. How is nitrogen and hydrogen obtained respectively?

nitrogen: fractional distillation of air; hydrogen: cracking of crude oil
nitrogen: cracking of crude oil; hydrogen: reacting metal with acid
nitrogen: cracking of crude oil; hydrogen: cracking of crude oil

questions.s:
The Haber process is carried out at 250 atmospheres and 450 °C.

According to the graph, at 250 atmospheres, the yield of ammonia is highest at 350 °C. What is the reason why the Haber process is carried out at 450 °C instead?
o: The low temperature requires expensive equipment to withstand the heat.
The rate of reaction would be much slower at 350 °C.
The high pressure causes a slower rate of reaction.
A low pressure would cause the gases to leak out.
